sonnet.problem: The opening card says Jesus 'drove demons out of a man.' That hands over 'demons', the right answer to the fill-in-the-blank on card 2.
sonnet.rule: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

sonnet.problem: This story card retells the list of no staff, no bag, no bread, no money, no second tunic right after card 7 asked about bread and money. It reuses an answer already shown and adds nothing new to move the passage along.
sonnet.rule: An answer shown on one card, right or wrong, isn't used again on a later card.

sonnet.problem: The question 'Others say ___ has appeared.' doesn't say who is being talked about or who 'others' are. It depends on card 16, which the baker can no longer see.
sonnet.rule: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

sonnet.problem: The question asks the baker to pick how John was killed (beheaded, stoned or crucified). That asks about the violent act itself.
sonnet.rule: Choice cards ask about the choices and results around them, never the act itself.

sonnet.problem: The true/false statement joins two claims: Herod asks who this man is, and he then gives up trying to see Jesus.
sonnet.rule: A true or false statement tests one claim.
